summary.name: Rekody
summary.one_liner: Rekody is a free, open-source, on-device voice dictation app for macOS that types your speech at the cursor in any app.
use_cases: dictating text into any Mac app
private voice notes without cloud upload
writing emails or documents by voice
command-line voice dictation via Homebrew CLI
summary.what_it_does: Hold the ⌥ Space shortcut to speak; words appear as you talk and the final text is inserted at the cursor when you release. A quick tap of the shortcut starts hands-free dictation that runs until you tap again, suited to longer dictation. The pill indicator shows which app you are typing into. Transcription runs on-device by default, with cloud engines available only as an opt-in using your own key. The page says the code is MIT-licensed on GitHub and that an open-source CLI is available.
notable: On-device transcription by default with no account, analytics, or audio saved
One native binary (~35 MB), not Electron, per the page
MIT-licensed open source with a CLI installable via Homebrew
caveats: Real-time streaming needs Apple Silicon; Intel Macs transcribe with Whisper
Speech models download once at setup, so initial setup needs network access
Cloud engines are optional and require your own API key
